messages:
Priya: Heads-up — MedSys (large healthcare SaaS) just surfaced a complex pricing ask and wants product input. They want a reserved capacity commit + a pool of burst credits for seasonal spikes. Also HIPAA requirements + audit logs. Can product weigh in on viable packaging + launch criteria?

Sam: need a few numbers to triage: expected sustained QPS, token volume, spike magnitude & duration, and whether they require private deployment or ok with Dedicated in our hosted offering.

Priya: baseline ~200 req/s, ~3M tokens/day. Month-end spikes to ~800 req/s (4x) for ~48–72 hrs. Willing to commit to 50% of peak for 6–12 months if we provide rollover credits and burst headroom. Requires 99.9% uptime SLA and audit logs; prefers VPC but will consider Dedicated if faster.

Jordan: sales input — customer is willing to sign if we give predictable unit economics. They asked for two options: (1) discounted per-token + reserved monthly fee + burst credits, (2) larger commit (12mo) with deeper discount and limited rollover. Wants simple math to present.

Maya: from an infra/productization perspective: Dedicated (hosted reserved GPU pool) fits well — we already have the networking/KMS hooks for HIPAA. Private (on-prem) is more work (8–10 wks integration). Bursting can be handled by a shared burst pool but we need policy + throttle rules.

Ken: finance — propose we model two SKUs: Core+Burst (monthly reserved capacity fee + capped burst credits, overage per-token at premium) and Commit+Credits (longer term commit with deeper blended per-token rate and limited rollover). Put discount bands and margin floor; recommend approvals for >25% discount.

Priya: to be actionable I need launch/acceptance criteria. What must be in place before we present pricing?

Sam: acceptance criteria (high level):
- Billing calc surfaced in Console (per-route token meter + expected monthly spend calc)
- Credits pool visible with rollover rules (e.g., up to 30 days)
- Autoscale + burst policy defined (max burst concurrency, fallback model variant)
- SLA doc (99.9% uptime commitment + escalation path)
- HIPAA-ready deployment option documented (Dedicated vs Private and timelines)

Jordan: negotiation levers to present: shorter pilot (3mo, lower commit) with option to convert to longer commit; early-payment discounts (1–3%); include 1–2 reference credits for onboarding support.

SalesBot: Internal pricing calc: https://internal.redwood/pricing-calc?deal=MEDSYS-PR1 (placeholder) :link: 

Maya: effort estimate: Console UI for credits + billing view (~2 sprints), autoscale + burst policy config (~1 sprint infra + ops), SLA/legal template + docs (~1 sprint). Cross-team ~3 sprints total to deliver MVP.

Ken: commercial ask — we need to model net unit economics for the two SKUs and show P&L at 50% commit and at 100% actual usage. I'll take the modeling but need the expected token mix (generation vs embedding) from the customer.

Priya: @Ken I'll send the token mix after the call. @Legal any HIPAA red flags we should surface early?

Legal: HIPAA requires BAAs and audit logging for PHI flows. If they want on-prem we need a different contract amendment. For Dedicated hosted we can do a BAA; ops controls and KMS are required.

Sam: product backlog items suggested:
- PACKAGING-427: Core+Burst SKU (billing + console + credits UX) — acceptance criteria per above
- PACKAGING-428: Commit+Credits blended rate + rollover rules + discount bands
- PACKAGING-429: SLA & HIPAA deployment runbook + sales one-pager
Please mark P1 if we agree to prioritize.

Priya: I recommend P1 for MedSys due to revenue + reference potential. Next steps: Jordan will present two options to customer this week; Sam/Maya/Ken will finalize numbers and delivery estimate; Legal to draft BAA checklist; I'll create the one-pager and link PACKAGING tickets.

Jordan: I can run the call Thurs 11am PT. Will align on the one-pager beforehand.

Priya: Great — thanks everyone. I'll create the tickets and assign owners. :thumbsup:
